title: The Ketef Hinnom silver scrolls

images.caption: The two silver scrolls (KH1 and KH2) after unrolling.

p: Two tiny rolled sheets of silver, worn as amulets, were found among the burial goods of a family tomb across the Hinnom Valley from Mount Zion. When they were finally unrolled, both turned out to carry, in old Hebrew script, a form of the priestly blessing of Numbers 6:24–26: “The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make His face shine upon you…”
They are the oldest known copies of words from the Hebrew Bible, several centuries older than the Dead Sea Scrolls. The divine name YHWH is written out in them.
facts: 1979, in a burial cave at Ketef Hinnom, Jerusalem
Around 600 BC, shortly before the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem
KH1 about 27 × 97 mm; KH2 about 11 × 39 mm
